answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each quill to a crystal of sunk reputation: every graded round raises the bond an identity must post next, so history gets progressively costlier to fake. A fresh clone starts at the cheapest tier but must climb the same crystal staircase, paying full price for each layer it skips; a vine of sibling identities is caught when their bonds and sudden joint silence trace one hand. Doubling a sybil set does not double cost, it squares it, because each extra clone must independently re-earn the confidence the honest identity already crystallized.
